prospect.name: David Pasco
prospect.location: United States, Eastern time zone; currently living in and selling the estate house he inherited
prospect.occupation: Not established — the question was never asked. He is full-time executor of his late aunt and uncle's estate, six years into liquidating a hoarded property, and is separately developing a web platform he describes as intended to 'reinvent the way the World Wide Web works'. Holds a 200-hour Kripalu yoga teaching certification but is not currently teaching.
prospect.family_status: Single. A long-term relationship ended when his then-partner joined what he describes as a fanatical religious group. His mother died of Alzheimer's and he cared for her until her death; he also cared for the aunt and uncle whose estate he now administers.
prospect.training_background: Certified yoga teacher via a month-long residential Kripalu immersion. Lost his practice for several years after the relationship ended, resumed roughly 19-20 months ago and now practises an hour a day six days a week, at what he describes as level two to three of five. Walks 8,000-10,000 steps a day on a treadmill at a 1.5 incline and about three miles an hour. Dry sauna five or six days a week for 20-25 minutes. Tai chi 10-15 minutes each morning from YouTube, started two weeks ago. Meditates twice daily for 20 minutes. Began kettlebell work roughly two weeks before the call with a 15lb bell, self-directed from Trevor's videos. Push-up attempts have repeatedly burned out. Lost 80lb once when younger and kept it off five or six years.
prospect.medical: Says he needs to lose 60-70lb, though the setter's note recorded 20-30. Congenital lower-limb issue — his legs turned outward at birth and he wore braces on both for the first six months of life, with a residual tendency he attributes to possible glute medius weakness. Uneven gait that worsens with distance or incline. Flat feet with feet 'always aching from walking'. Formerly severe acid reflux, now resolved without prescriptions, but frequent bloating after eating. Severe chronic sleep disruption: falls asleep between 9:30pm and midnight and wakes at 1am or 3am unable to return to sleep for hours, with periods of nightmares. Describes himself as in a 'constant fight or flight state' and speculates 'probably like an unlimited cortisol kind of situation'. Extensive therapy history. Ongoing severe psychological distress from six years of administering an estate in which he discovered his late uncle was a Nazi collector and a child abuser, requiring him to repeatedly identify and destroy material.

notable.note: The most difficult call in the batch to read and the one carrying the most sensitive disclosure. The prospect described six years administering an estate in which he discovered his late uncle was a Nazi collector and a child abuser, requiring him to repeatedly find and destroy material; alongside chronic sleep disruption with nightmares, a self-described constant fight-or-flight state, social isolation and lost confidence. The rep handled it with real care — he listened without deflecting, asked 'And why is that?' when doubt surfaced, and refused to push at the close ('let's take a chill pill. Because the last thing I want is to put you in a financial distress') — but he also positioned the programme as part of the psychological repair, with no suggestion of any other kind of support, and then took a $100 deposit. Two hard commercial findings sit alongside that. First, the renewal rate was disclosed unprompted at $3,000 for a further six months, half the initial price — and that figure is the same one quoted as an initial price to Bennu Kham Ra Ankh Aten four days earlier, which suggests the $3,000 in that call may be a renewal rate being used as a discount. Second, this is the third appearance of the $100 refundable deposit in this batch and the second time it was paid.
